edges.description: Knockout mice have audiogenic seizures and, after an aversive conditioning stimulus, reduced brain weight, hippocampal and midbrain atrophy and thinner cortex.
edges.limitations: Learning and anxiety behaviour were normal at baseline, and the brain atrophy appeared only in stimulus-exposed mice, unlike the constitutive microcephaly and severe intellectual disability of patients; corpus callosum was not reported.

nodes.description: Impaired growth and development of the brain, seen in patients as microcephaly and a thin or absent corpus callosum. It is the endpoint both hypotheses share. The cellular steps linking either EEF1D function to this outcome have not been defined.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive intellectual disability caused by compound heterozygous variants of the EEF1D gene in a Chinese family.
evidence.snippet: The primary clinical features observed in these cases were GDD/ID (10/10), including severe ID (5/5), microcephaly (10/10), no language expression (8/8), inability to walk alone (7/7), epilepsy (4/5), short stature (7/7), hypotonia (3/7), and hypertonia (4/7).

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating, splice-site or missense variants in EEF1D. The first variants reported, in consanguineous families from Iran and Turkey, truncate the exon unique to the long isoform and so remove eEF1BdeltaL while sparing the short translation-factor isoforms. Variants reported later lie in the C-terminal guanine nucleotide exchange domain that all isoforms share. Most patients are homozygous; one Chinese patient was compound heterozygous for a splice variant and a long-isoform nonsense variant. The two activities bound below are those of the two EEF1D products, the exchange activity of the short isoforms and the DNA-binding transcription factor activity of eEF1BdeltaL; which one a given variant removes depends on where it lies, and the two downstream nodes carry that distinction.

nodes.description: The short eEF1Bdelta isoforms are part of the eEF1B complex that exchanges GDP for GTP on eEF1A, releasing it from the ribosome so elongation can continue. Variants in the C-terminal exchange domain, shared by every isoform, are proposed to impair this step and so protein synthesis.

evidence.reference_title: Expanding the spectrum of EEF1D neurodevelopmental disorders: Biallelic variants in the guanine exchange domain.
evidence.snippet: The eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1A (eEF1A) delivers aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosome, while the eEF1B complex acts as a guanine exchange factor (GEF) of GTP for GDP indirectly catalyzing the release of eEF1A from the ribosome.

evidence.reference_title: The role of translation elongation factor eEF1 subunits in neurodevelopmental disorders.
evidence.snippet: However, mutations in the genes encoding these subunits EEF1B2 (eEF1Bα), EEF1D (eEF1Bδ), and VARS (valyl-tRNA synthetase) have also now been identified as causes of neurodevelopmental disorders.

evidence.reference_title: Characterisation of translation elongation factor eEF1B subunit expression in mammalian cells and tissues and co-localisation with eEF1A2.
evidence.snippet: We show that ablation of any of the subunits in human cell lines has a small but significant impact on cell viability and cycling.

nodes.description: eEF1BdeltaL is a nuclear isoform that cooperates with HSF1 to induce heat-shock-element genes and binds NRF2 to induce heme oxygenase 1. Its loss is proposed to blunt the stress response of developing neurons.

nodes.description: Without eEF1BdeltaL, the brain is less able to withstand external stressors. In long-isoform knockout mice this appears as audiogenic seizures and as brain atrophy that follows an aversive stimulus but is absent at baseline. Whether the same vulnerability operates in patients has not been tested. The node belongs to the heat-shock hypothesis only.
